blurb: Small molecules and degraders, antibodies, peptides and enzymes, oligonucleotides, vaccines, gene therapy, and cell therapy, with what each costs to develop, make, and dose.
question: What should this therapy be?
title: Therapeutic Modalities: A Practical Reference
lede: Modality choice settles more of a drug program than target choice does. It decides which targets are reachable at all, whether a patient doses daily or once in a lifetime, whether cost of goods is $2 a dose or $200,000, and how much regulatory precedent comes free. This guide catalogs {{N_ENTRIES}} modalities across seven families, with the development costs, dosing intervals, manufacturing costs, and approval counts that decide between them.

groupBlurbs.Small molecules: chemical matter that crosses the membrane
groupBlurbs.Targeted degraders: destroy the protein instead of blocking it
groupBlurbs.Radiopharmaceuticals: deliver a radioisotope to the tumor
groupBlurbs.Engineered antibody formats: reshaped for payload, size, or half-life
groupBlurbs.Peptides: short chains between small molecule and protein
groupBlurbs.Replacement proteins: supply a protein the patient cannot make
groupBlurbs.Immune modulators: turn an immune response up or down
groupBlurbs.Gene silencing: cut the amount of protein a cell makes
groupBlurbs.Coding and binding oligos: supply a message or bind a target directly
groupBlurbs.Genetic vaccines: deliver instructions and let the body make antigen
groupBlurbs.In vivo gene therapy: dose the patient and edit in place
groupBlurbs.Ex vivo gene therapy: modify cells outside the body, then return them
groupBlurbs.Engineered T cells: redirect T cells at a chosen target
groupBlurbs.Natural and derived cells: expanded or differentiated rather than redirected
groupBlurbs.Living agents: viruses and bacteria as the therapy

facets.label: Reaches
facets.tip: What the modality can act on. Cell surface covers receptors and secreted proteins, which any binder can reach. Intracellular means it gets through the membrane to a protein inside. RNA means it binds or destroys a transcript. Genome means it changes DNA the cell will keep. Whole cells means the target is a cell population rather than a molecule, and Pathogens means bacteria, viruses, or fungi. Directional: an antibody conjugated to something that internalizes is still tagged as surface, because the binding event is what has to happen outside.

facets.label: Dosing
facets.tip: How often a patient takes it once on maintenance, not during induction: Daily includes anything from once to several times a day · Weekly covers weekly to biweekly · Monthly covers monthly to quarterly · Yearly is once or twice a year · Once means a single administration intended to last for years. Dosing interval drives adherence, cost per patient-year, and how much of the price a payer will accept up front.

facets.label: COGS/dose
facets.tip: Roughly what one dose costs to manufacture and release at commercial scale, counting drug substance, fill-finish, QC, and amortized facility. This is cost of goods, not price, and the two are barely related in this industry: a $2 cost of goods routinely sells for $500, and a $200,000 cost of goods sells for $3M. Directional, and it moves a long way with batch size and how much of the plant sits idle.

facets.label: Maturity
facets.tip: How settled the modality is in drug development: Early = research and early clinical, nothing approved and the format is still moving · Emerging = approvals exist but the playbook is still being written · Proven = a well-understood path many programs have walked · Default = what a program picks for a suitable target unless there is a specific reason not to.

facets.label: Approvals
facets.tip: Roughly how many products of this exact modality FDA has approved, which is the cheapest available proxy for how predictable the review will be: None = no approval yet, so the first filing writes the guidance · Few = 1–4 products, enough to know the path exists · Several = 5–20, so reviewers have settled expectations · Many = more than 20, and the questions are known before you ask them. Counts move, so treat the band rather than the number as the fact.
